answer: Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 373 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, as the vertex funding graph is rebuilt from the kernel history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 373 bonds yet holds one position, and the mesa report publishes the merged exposure. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
